bluf: Genie Goals is a paid social specialist filed under Europe whose public record, at this compile, is three LinkedIn company page ads about Meta's Andromeda update. Its site failed TLS handshakes on both hostnames and the Internet Archive's 2026 capture holds only a 403 error page, so the record is silent on services, clients, offices, ownership and pricing; confidence is low. It is talking to Meta advertisers about creative strategy after Andromeda, fronted by its Head of Paid Social. Where it is going: the record cannot say. The thing a rival should know: the Horus read scores it a Headwind of -74.3 on a single line the platforms are absorbing.

The positioning line is what its LinkedIn ads present: a paid social team unpacking Meta's Andromeda update and what it means for creative strategy. In plain words, Genie Goals sells Meta ad buying and creative strategy, and its current pitch is that Andromeda changed how creative has to be planned. There is no headline claim, no service list, no proprietary product and no partner in the record, because nothing beyond the ads was reachable.

The sold mix is one line: paid social, scored 2 on the evidence that all three LinkedIn company ads discuss Meta's Andromeda update and feature its Head of Paid Social, the only capability with a score above 0. Breadth is 1. Paid search, programmatic, creator, data and measurement, CRM, SEO, AI search and AI automation all score 0, which reads as unobserved rather than absent: the site could not be read, so the record cannot say what else it sells. The ads themselves are two videos and one event, seen at the 2026-09-27 check.

AI posture: none in the record; the ads talk about Meta's own ranking system, not about AI tooling of its own. Moves: the list is empty, with no news, case studies or jobs captured. Pricing signals: none. Conspicuously absent for a paid social specialist of its kind: any measurement or incrementality line, any creative volume evidence beyond the three ads, any first party data offer, any platform beyond Meta, and any ICP or vertical, since the record lists none. The one observed fact is that it advertises to marketers on LinkedIn about Meta creative strategy, which places it, inferred from the ads alone, as a Meta first buyer selling to teams that noticed Andromeda.
clients:
The record lists no client type, no ICP, no vertical and no office; the region is Europe by filing, and the second LinkedIn ad says it sent its Head of Paid Social undercover at Meta's London offices, the only place name in the record. The needs read is empty: 0 clients, 0 observed, 0 named only, no mix, no shared clients and no evidence types, because the case study and client pages could not be fetched and the Internet Archive holds only the 403 page.

What can be inferred, said as such: the ads are aimed at advertisers who buy Meta creative and worry about the Andromeda update, so the buyer the agency wants is a brand or in house team with Meta spend and a creative pipeline, and the need it sells to is paid performance with a brand and creative edge, inferred from the ads and nothing else. No client name appears anywhere in the record, so nothing can be marked as shared with another tracked agency and nothing is names only: the book is unobserved rather than thin.

What the base needs next: the Horus read gives Genie Goals no tailwind and makes KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) its exposures, both driven by paid social. It is very likely, with low confidence given the empty record, that its Meta clients will buy creative volume and measurement rather than hours, since the execution layer it sells is the one Meta's own systems are taking.

openings:
The strongest opening is structural. Genie Goals sells one line, paid social execution and creative strategy for Meta, and the Horus read makes that line its whole exposure: a Headwind of -74.3 with no tailwind, driven by KJ4. It is very likely, with moderate confidence on the read but low on the record, that a rival selling Meta creative volume plus incrementality measurement, priced on outputs, can take its clients as Meta's automation absorbs the buying hours. Falsifier: a readable Genie Goals site showing measurement, first party data or multi platform lines that the ads do not.

Second, no public pricing model: an outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot hold in public. Third, the empty record itself: with the site unreachable and no client, case or office on record, a rival that simply publishes cases and a working site has more proof than this record holds. The Monsoon read is Doldrums at 36.7 with automation overlapping 100% of the movable hours, so an offshore undercut is the wrong lead: the read says these hours are automated, not relocated, and the rival's pitch is the automation itself. Every judgment here rests on three ads.
